title: Helpful assistant or fruitful facilitator? Investigating how personas affect language model behavior

bias_targets.methodology: Measured by calculating bias scores on the BBQ question-answering benchmark (comparing answers in ambiguous vs. disambiguated contexts), measuring toxicity and offensiveness ratings on tweets written in African-American English (AAE) or targeting Black people, and analyzing disparate model refusal rates when assigned race-specific personas.

Measured by calculating bias scores on the BBQ question-answering benchmark, evaluating self-reported attitude scores (e.g., traditionalism, language purism) across gender personas, and analyzing disparate model refusal rates when assigned different gender personas.

Measured by calculating bias scores on the BBQ question-answering benchmark to evaluate bias against groups like gay, bisexual, and pansexual individuals, and analyzing disparate model refusal rates when prompted to adopt sexuality-specific personas.

Measured by calculating bias scores on the BBQ question-answering benchmark to evaluate bias against groups like Jewish, Muslim, Hindu, Christian, and Atheist individuals, and evaluating changes in task performance and attitude scores when models adopt religious personas.

Evaluated using the BBQ question-answering benchmark which highlights biases regarding socioeconomic status, and by comparing the task performance and attitude scores of different social class personas (e.g., upper-class vs. middle-class).

Evaluated by analyzing disparate model refusal rates when assigned specific political figures or ideologies, and measuring differences in self-reported attitudes (e.g., empathy, altruism, racist beliefs) across ideological personas.
